subject: econ
source: IB Diploma Programme Economics guide (first assessment 2022) — HL, DP1: Units 1–3 with HL-only content (theory of the firm, quantitative methods)

weeks.topic: What is economics? Scarcity, choice and opportunity cost
objectives: Explain scarcity and the basic economic problem
Identify factors of production and their rewards
Illustrate opportunity cost with a production possibilities curve

weeks.topic: Economic methodology and the nine key concepts
objectives: Distinguish positive and normative statements
Explain the role of models, assumptions and ceteris paribus
Apply the key concepts (scarcity, efficiency, equity, sustainability…)

weeks.topic: Economic systems and the circular flow of income
objectives: Compare market, planned and mixed economies
Draw the circular flow with leakages and injections
Outline the evolution of economic thinking (Smith to behavioural)

weeks.topic: Demand: the law of demand and its determinants — HL: linear demand functions
objectives: Explain the law of demand (income and substitution effects)
Distinguish movements along and shifts of the demand curve
Identify non-price determinants of demand
Calculate and plot linear demand functions (Qd = a − bP)

weeks.topic: Supply and competitive market equilibrium — HL: solving equilibrium with functions
objectives: Explain the law of supply and its determinants
Analyse excess demand and excess supply
Explain the signalling and incentive functions of price
Solve for equilibrium price and quantity from linear functions

weeks.topic: Consumer and producer surplus and allocative efficiency — HL: calculating surplus areas
objectives: Define consumer and producer surplus
Explain allocative efficiency where MB = MC
Show community surplus on diagrams
Calculate consumer and producer surplus from diagrams and functions

weeks.topic: Behavioural economics: critique of the rational consumer
objectives: Explain assumptions of rational consumer choice
Analyse biases: availability, anchoring, framing, defaults
Evaluate nudge theory and choice architecture

weeks.topic: Price elasticity of demand (PED) — HL: PED along a linear demand curve
objectives: Calculate and interpret PED values
Explain the determinants of PED
Link PED to total revenue and firm pricing
Explain why PED varies along a straight-line demand curve

weeks.topic: PES, YED and primary versus manufactured goods
objectives: Calculate and interpret PES and YED
Distinguish normal, inferior, necessity and luxury goods
Explain why commodities have low PED and PES

weeks.topic: Government intervention: indirect taxes and subsidies — HL: tax incidence calculations
objectives: Analyse specific and ad valorem taxes
Analyse the effects of subsidies
Evaluate the impact on consumers, producers and government
Calculate tax incidence, government revenue and welfare loss

weeks.topic: Price controls: price ceilings and price floors — HL: price control calculations
objectives: Analyse maximum prices such as rent control
Analyse minimum prices and minimum wages
Evaluate shortages, surpluses and parallel markets
Calculate shortages, surpluses and welfare effects of price controls

weeks.topic: Market failure: negative externalities
objectives: Explain market failure as a divergence of private and social costs
Draw negative production and consumption externality diagrams
Apply to pollution, tobacco and alcohol

weeks.topic: Positive externalities and responses to externalities
objectives: Analyse positive production and consumption externalities
Evaluate carbon taxes, tradable permits and regulation
Assess subsidies and awareness campaigns

weeks.topic: Common pool resources, public goods and sustainability
objectives: Explain the tragedy of the commons
Analyse public goods and the free-rider problem
Discuss collective self-governance and international cooperation

weeks.topic: Term 1 review: microeconomic foundations and market failure
objectives: Practise Paper 1 part (a) and (b) answers with diagrams
Revise elasticities and government intervention
Self-assess definitions and diagram labelling

weeks.topic: Business objectives and CSR — HL: costs and revenues
objectives: Compare profit, revenue and growth maximization
Explain satisficing and CSR
Analyse short-run cost curves and the law of diminishing returns
Calculate TR, AR and MR and identify profit-maximizing output

weeks.topic: The market's inability to achieve equity — HL: asymmetric information
objectives: Explain why markets can lead to unequal outcomes
Analyse policies addressing inequality in access to goods
Explain adverse selection and moral hazard
Evaluate screening, signalling and regulation

weeks.topic: IA portfolio: writing a microeconomics commentary — HL: perfect competition
objectives: Select a recent news article and link it to a key concept
Use diagrams and terminology accurately
Plan analysis and evaluation within the word limit
Analyse short-run and long-run equilibrium in perfect competition

weeks.topic: Measuring economic activity: GDP, GNI and real values — HL: monopoly
objectives: Distinguish GDP, GNI, nominal and real values
Calculate real GDP using a price deflator
Explain limitations of GDP data
Analyse monopoly equilibrium, barriers to entry and natural monopoly

weeks.topic: Measuring well-being beyond GDP — HL: oligopoly and monopolistic competition
objectives: Compare GDP per capita and PPP
Evaluate HDI, OECD Better Life Index and happiness indices
Analyse monopolistic competition
Use game theory to explain collusion and price wars

weeks.topic: Aggregate demand and its components — HL: market power and competition policy
objectives: Define AD and its components C + I + G + (X − M)
Explain the shape of the AD curve
Explain market power as a market failure
Evaluate competition policy and regulation

weeks.topic: Short-run aggregate supply and macroeconomic equilibrium
objectives: Explain SRAS and its determinants
Show short-run equilibrium, recessionary and inflationary gaps
Analyse supply shocks

weeks.topic: Long-run aggregate supply — HL: the Keynesian model in depth
objectives: Compare the vertical LRAS and the Keynesian AS curve
Explain full-employment output
Analyse shifts in LRAS
Analyse equilibrium in the three sections of the Keynesian AS curve

weeks.topic: Macroeconomic objective: low unemployment — HL: natural rate of unemployment
objectives: Calculate the unemployment rate
Explain structural, frictional, seasonal and cyclical unemployment
Evaluate costs of unemployment
Explain the natural rate and its relation to LRAS

weeks.topic: Low and stable inflation — HL: constructing a weighted price index
objectives: Explain demand-pull and cost-push inflation
Evaluate costs of inflation and deflation
Interpret the consumer price index
Construct a weighted price index and calculate inflation rates

weeks.topic: Macroeconomic objective: economic growth — HL: Phillips curve
objectives: Explain causes of growth using PPC and LRAS
Evaluate consequences of growth for living standards and environment
Calculate growth rates
Analyse the short-run and long-run Phillips curve

weeks.topic: Mid-year exams: microeconomics and introductory macroeconomics
objectives: Complete timed Paper 1 and Paper 2 questions
Apply diagrams under exam conditions
Review feedback and set targets

weeks.topic: Equity: income and wealth inequality and poverty
objectives: Interpret Lorenz curves and Gini coefficients
Distinguish absolute and relative poverty
Explain causes of inequality

weeks.topic: Taxation and policies to reduce inequality — HL: calculating tax rates
objectives: Compare progressive, regressive and proportional taxes
Evaluate transfer payments and universal basic income
Discuss Bolsa Família as a real-world example
Calculate average and marginal tax rates

weeks.topic: Environmental sustainability and government debt
objectives: Explain sustainability as a macroeconomic objective
Distinguish budget deficit and government debt
Evaluate consequences of high public debt

weeks.topic: Demand-side policies: monetary policy — HL: real interest rates and money creation
objectives: Explain the role and goals of central banks
Analyse interest rate changes and quantitative easing
Calculate real interest rates
Explain money creation by commercial banks

weeks.topic: Demand-side policies: fiscal policy — HL: Keynesian multiplier
objectives: Analyse expansionary and contractionary fiscal policy
Explain automatic stabilizers and discretionary policy
Evaluate crowding out and time lags
Calculate the multiplier from MPC and marginal propensities to withdraw

weeks.topic: Supply-side policies: market-based and interventionist
objectives: Analyse labour market, deregulation and privatization policies
Analyse investment in education, infrastructure and R&D
Evaluate effects on growth and inequality

weeks.topic: IA portfolio: planning a macroeconomics commentary
objectives: Choose an article from a different unit and key concept
Apply AD/AS diagrams to the article
Draft an evaluation that weighs stakeholders

weeks.topic: Policy conflicts and trade-offs — HL: Phillips curve applications
objectives: Analyse growth versus inflation and growth versus environment
Evaluate the effectiveness of policy mixes
Apply to Brazil's recent macro data
Use SRPC and LRPC to evaluate the inflation–unemployment trade-off

weeks.topic: End-of-year exams: Units 1–3 — HL: Paper 3 practice
objectives: Complete timed Paper 1 essays and Paper 2 data response
Use accurate diagrams and real-world examples
Reflect on strengths and gaps
Attempt quantitative HL Paper 3 questions

weeks.topic: Year review: consolidating micro and macro; summer IA plan
objectives: Map links between micro and macro concepts
Correct exam errors with model diagrams
Plan the next IA commentary
